bible.title: Winter Mountainside Cabin
bible.intent: A secluded timber cabin on a snowy mountainside at winter dusk. Follow the conifer trail into a compact furnished home: entry storage, kitchen and dining area, a living room around the stone hearth, and a sleeping loft with a desk. The deck and forest viewpoint open toward layered mountain ridges and a distant lake. Preserve the welcoming contrast of warm interiors and cool snow, convincing human scale, detailed materials and a continuous route through the whole setting.
bible.rules:
SETTING AND COMPOSITION
Keep one coherent cabin, surrounding forest, snowy approach, woodland loop, deck and lake viewpoint. Maintain the relationship between the dark timber exterior, stone base, warm glazing, cool snow and layered mountain silhouettes. Protect useful views at ordinary standing height as well as overview compositions. Distant ridges and lake scenery are not routes to explore.

CABIN AND HABITATION
Keep the exterior shell, stairs, floor levels, loft and roof structure consistent inside and outside. Preserve usable entry storage, kitchen, dining, living, sleeping, work and loft storage areas. Maintain clear door swings and stair landings. Main circulation should be at least 1.10 m wide, secondary and bedside access at least 0.90 m, stair landings at least 1.20 m, and occupied routes at least 2.10 m high. Furniture, lamps, props, walls and foundations must visibly meet their supports.

FOREST AND WALKING
Retain the substantial 360-tree forest and its seven conifer families. Keep readable snowy paths, a clear return route and the viewpoint's lake sightline. Outdoor paths target a 1.8 m clear tread and a 3.5 m vegetation keep-out. Aim for crossfall at most 5 degrees, sustained grades at most 8 degrees and short grades at most 12 degrees. Check real terrain triangles and collider support after edits; visual terrain alone does not establish walkability. Keep the viewpoint seat grounded, its cap level, and its standing approach clear.

MATERIALS AND LIGHT
Use distinct dark structural timber, restrained warm interior wood, matte neutral wall areas, rugged stone, dark metal, readable glass and soft woven textiles. Keep wood grain and textile detail at believable scale. Snow should collect plausibly on ground, rock and branches. Preserve readable lamp housings, restrained hearth embers and warm practical light against cool environmental fill; brightness must not erase material detail. Judge both the interior and outward views before changing exposure or lighting.

TRAILHEAD AND EDITING
Keep the winter stone trailhead and empty World board usable at the origin. Essential cabin and route supports belong to the world layer and must remain usable when the origin is hidden. Read the current world before editing and stage complete proposals with supported Holodeck tools. Save placement and material changes as revisions; runtime door movement and camera activity are separate from saved layout. Exact GLBs in this example support scene editing; original procedural asset programs are supplied separately through the companion Kiln asset pack.

VERIFICATION
These rules describe design intent, not a performance guarantee. Recheck the arrival, forest loop, exterior stairs, both cabin doors, interior stairs, loft, deck, viewpoint and return after relevant changes. Confirm material appearance from inside and outside, supported clearances, and stable rendering on the actual renderer. Keep visual review, host queries, walking observations and performance measurements distinct. Do not replace an unresolved route or rendering issue with a claimed pass.
